title: Find the Minimum Amount of Time to Brew Potions
summary: Given two integer arrays, skill and mana, of lengths n and m respectively, you are to determine the minimum amount of time required for n wizards to sequentially brew m potions.
statement: Given two integer arrays, skill and mana, of lengths n and m respectively, you are to determine the minimum amount of time required for n wizards to sequentially brew m potions. Each potion requires a specific amount of time to be processed by each wizard, with the time for the ith wizard on the jth potion calculated as skill[i] * mana[j]. The potions must be passed to the next wizard immediately after the current one finishes, ensuring that the timing is synchronized.
constraints: skill and mana are nonempty positive-integer arrays.
Every potion visits all wizards in order; wizard i takes skill[i]*mana[j] time.
A potion must pass immediately between wizards, and no wizard may process two potions simultaneously; minimize the final completion time.
reference_solution:
def minimum_synchronized_potion_time(skill,mana):
    finish=[0]*len(skill)
    for power in mana:
        current=0
        for index,value in enumerate(skill):current=max(current,finish[index])+value*power
        finish[-1]=current
        for index in range(len(skill)-2,-1,-1):finish[index]=finish[index+1]-skill[index+1]*power
    return finish[-1]

hints: Once a potion starts, its no-wait finish times are fixed offsets; its start must satisfy every wizard’s previous finish.
Simulate the earliest feasible schedule and back-propagate each new potion’s synchronized timeline.
Sweep wizards using max(current arrival, prior finish), set the last finish, then subtract processing times backward to recover earlier finishes.
The forward maximum finds the smallest start respecting all resource conflicts, and delaying it could only delay the final answer.
